newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha stable, shrugging off weaker crudes.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha stable, shrugging off weaker crudes.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices held steady in subdued trade on Monday after shrugging off Friday's bearish overseas crude markets, traders said.
Asian naphtha was firmly supported by healthy regional fundamentals, they said.

Bids for second-half April open-spec naphtha were heard at $236.00 per tonne, and first-half May was bid at $231.00. Offer levels were notionally assessed at $237.00 for second-half April, and $232.00 for first-half May.
In naphtha spreads, first-half May/second-half May was traded at plus $4.00 on Friday.
The one-month spread from first-half April was discussed at plus $10.00/11.00, little changed from levels in late Friday.

In middle distillates, a Japanese oil firm said it had bought 30,000 tonnes of dual purpose kerosene for mid-March delivery. The price was unavailable. The company said this would be its last kerosene purchase for this winter.

Japan's kerosene stockpiles at the end of January grew by 30 percent from a year earlier, and gas oil inventories by 25 percent due to mild winter weather, the Ministry of International Trade and Industry said.
